newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end soft as foreigners stay away.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end soft as foreigners stay away.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed weaker Wednesday in slim volume as foreign investors stayed away, brokers said.
The market, which has been depressed for weeks because of the economy's slow growth, was not likely to show signs of recovery this week, they added.
Wednesday, the General Index fell 0.7 percent to 1,481.1 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.2 percent to 2,088.4 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
"The negative trend is because foreigners are absent as they see they can make profits more easily on exchanges like New York's," said Manuel Torres of local brokerage Finvest.
Wednesday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru dragged the market down, closing down 0.37 percent at 5.39 soles, on a preliminary count of 468,014 million shares.
Due to rules introduced last week, stocks can continue to be traded, but their prices are fixed one hour before the end of the day's session.
Brokers and stock exchange officials have said the market's indices will only vary slightly in this final hour.
When prices were fixed Monday at 1700 local time/2200 GMT, there had been 1,359 trades in volume estimated at 17.5 million soles ($6.8 million), brokers said.
